extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage. The dataset contains 107,785 question-answer pairs on 536 articles.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.citeAs: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, and Percy Liang. 2016. SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. In Proceedings of the 2016 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 2383–2392.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: (1) curating passages from Wikipedia articles, (2) crowdsourcing question-answers on those passages using the Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend, and (3) obtaining additional answers for development and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles were used as the source of passages. The top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia were obtained using Project Nayuki's Wikipedia's internal PageRanks, from which 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random. Individual paragraphs were extracted from these articles, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters, resulting in 23,215 paragraphs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: From each of the 536 Wikipedia articles, individual paragraphs were extracted, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. The result was 23,215 paragraphs. The articles were partitioned randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: From Wikipedia articles, individual paragraphs were extracted, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of each paragraph. Questions had to be entered in a text field, and answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph. Workers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words, without copying word phrases from the paragraph. For additional answers, crowdworkers were shown only the questions along with the paragraphs and asked to select the shortest span in the paragraph that answered the question. If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To get an indication of human performance and make evaluation more robust, at least 2 additional answers were obtained for each question in the development and test sets. Human performance was assessed by treating the second answer to each question as the human prediction, and keeping the other answers as ground truth answers. Mismatch occurred mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements about the answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 answers per question (1 original answer plus at least 2 additional answers for development and test sets)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP was used to generate constituency parses and POS tags for automatic categorization of answers.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper describes SQuAD v1.0. Over the last four months (since June 2016), improvements have been witnessed from more sophisticated models. Results on v1.1 are mentioned as similar to v1.0.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The model performance worsens with increasing complexity of answer types and syntactic divergence between the question and the sentence containing the answer. The model performs best on dates and other numbers, and is challenged more on other named entities because there are many more plausible candidates. The model performs worst on other answer types (adjective phrases, verb phrases, clauses), which together form 47.6% of the dataset. With lexicalized features, the model significantly overfits the training set.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The span constraint on answers means that questions with span-based answers are more constrained than the more interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests. The automatic candidate answer generation approach using constituency parses places an effective ceiling on accuracy at 77.3%, as only 77.3% of the correct answers in the development set are constituents.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is partitioned into training set (80%), development set (10%), and test set (10%). It is designed for training and evaluating reading comprehension models. The dataset presents a good challenge problem for future research in machine comprehension of text.
